claims.statement: The paper says Tom Allen was born at Birmingham, England, in 1841.
claims.excerpt: Who was born at Birmingham, England, in 1841, and is consequently twenty-eight years of age.

claims.statement: The paper gives Tom Allen's age as 28 at the time of the fight.
claims.excerpt: in 1841, and is consequently twenty-eight years of age

claims.statement: Tom Allen had been in the United States about eighteen months, and this was his first fight in the country.
claims.excerpt: He has been in this country eighteen months and this was his first fight in this country

claims.statement: In England Tom Allen had established a reputation as a hard hitter and a man of excellent science.
claims.excerpt: in England he had established his reputation as a hard hitter, and a man of excellent science

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Waggoner, one of his principal battles in England.
claims.excerpt: His principal battles were with Waggoner, White Clark, Tony Gould, Bingey Rose, J. Parkinson, P. Price, George Jils [?], Joe Goss and Bob Smith—the latter a colored man, who won the fight.

claims.excerpt: His principal battles were with Waggoner, White Clark, Tony Gould, Bingey Rose, J. Parkinson, P. Price, George Jils [?], Joe Goss and Bob Smith—the latter a colored man, who won the fight.

claims.statement: Bob Smith, a colored man, beat Tom Allen in one of Allen's principal battles in England.
claims.excerpt: His principal battles were with Waggoner, White Clark, Tony Gould, Bingey Rose, J. Parkinson, P. Price, George Jils [?], Joe Goss and Bob Smith—the latter a colored man, who won the fight.

claims.statement: Tom Allen and Bill Davis fought a prize fight on Chouteau Island, near Rhodes' Point, about twelve miles above the city.
claims.excerpt: The much talked of prize fight between Tom Allen and Bill Davis took place yesterday afternoon on Chouteau island, near Rhodes' point, about twelve miles above the city.

claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Bill Davis in 43 rounds lasting 41 minutes.
claims.excerpt: The battle was won by Allen in 41 minutes and 43 rounds

claims.statement: Bill Ryall and Tom Kelley were Tom Allen's seconds in the fight with Bill Davis.
claims.excerpt: The seconds of Davis were Mike McCoole and Wm. Blake, while Wm. Ryall and Tom Kelley, were the seconds of Allen

claims.statement: Tom Allen claimed he had been in active training for only nine days before the fight with Bill Davis.
claims.excerpt: as he claims to have been in active training only nine days

claims.statement: After the fight Tom Allen collected a handsome contribution for Bill Davis.
claims.excerpt: had been around and collected a handsome contribution for Davis

claims.statement: After the fight Tom Allen challenged Charles Gallagher to fight him in five weeks for $1,000.
claims.excerpt: You are a coward, and I will fight you in five weeks for $1000.

claims.statement: A $50 forfeit was put up for a fight within five weeks for $500 a side between Charles Gallagher and Tom Allen or Tom Kelley.
claims.excerpt: putting up fifty dollars forfeit for a fight within five weeks for $500 a side

claims.statement: Gallagher's backer said Gallagher would fight either Tom Allen or Tom Kelley.
claims.excerpt: Gallagher's backer stating that his man would fight either Allen or Kelley

claims.statement: As the boat neared the city, Tom Allen and Charles Gallagher nearly fought in the cabin, and the crowd kept them apart.
claims.excerpt: Gallagher "went for him," but the crowd interfered, and the pugilists were kept apart.

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: What kind of a fighter is that?

quotes.speaker: Tom Allen
quotes.text: You are a blarsted, bloody coward.
